TUMexchange bar comparison

Compare historical selection scores and explore TUM's partner requirements. Filter by degree and subject, or search for a university, city, or practical detail.

Interpretation

What the bars mean

This is a normalized historical selection-ratio indicator under a linear bar-width model. A full bar is assigned 100%; half the calibrated width is 50%. “No applications” is explicitly assigned 100%. This is not an individual admission probability and is not a grade-based prediction yet.

Australian National University (ANU) Canberra ACT · AustraliaShow 12 information sections: languages, deadlines, semester dates and moreHide detailed information BachelorMaster
14 eligible subject areas, listed belowChecked 2026-09-16
Level
Undergraduate / Bachelor
Postgraduate / Master
Website
Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Campus
Canberra
Semester Dates
Semester 2: July to November
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Semester 1: February to June
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
Study cycles are broadly similar to the German structure (Bachelor/Master).
Continuous Assessment: Weekly essays, presentations, mid-term exams, etc. account for 40–60% of the final grade.
Large lectures and small seminars (tutorials or labs): Attendance and active participation are expected/graded.
Full course load 24 ANU units per semester (typically 4 courses at 6 units each).
Minimum course load 18 ANU units per semester with approval from TUM and ANU.
Course catalogue and grading system is available on ANU's Fact Sheet
Admission Requirements
4.0/7.0 GPA ~ minimum 2,7 at TUM
Language Requirements
English: B2
Official English Language Test Results two years from the date of application: IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge C1 Advanced
Completion of a minimum 3 year Bachelor degree or a minimum 2 year Master degree taught and assessed entirely in English. Certificate issued in English, printed on official headed paper and duly signed.
A minimum of two years of full-time (or equivalent) education within the last four years taught and assessed entirely in English. Certificate issued in English, printed on official headed paper and duly signed.
Admission to ANU's undergraduate program: German Abitur achieved no more than two years prior to the date of application with a numerical grade of 3/‘befriedigend’ in English.
Additional Information
On-campus accommodation is guaranteed for all exchange students who apply for such an accommodation
Application Deadlines at Host University
Stays starting in July: April 1
Stays starting in February: November 1 (of previous year)

Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Campus
Macquarie Park / North Ryde (15 kilometers northwest of Sydney's city center)
Semester Dates
Semester 2: July to November
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Semester 1: February to June
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
Study cycles are broadly similar to the German structure (Bachelor/Master).
Continuous Assessment: Weekly essays, presentations, mid-term exams, etc. account for 40–60% of the final grade.
Large lectures and small seminars (tutorials or labs): Attendance and active participation are expected/graded.
Full-time enrolment at MQ in the study abroad program is 3 to 4 units per session.
MQ's Course Handbook: Provides unit overviews, levels, offerings.
MQ's Course Handbook
Admission Requirements
A Weighted Average Mark (WAM) of 60
Weighted Average Mark
Academic Restrictions
Closed Units: Formerly known as restricted units, these units are not accessible to Study Abroad and Exchange students.
Closed Units
Language Requirements
English: B2
IELTS, TOEFL, Cambridge, PTE
Abitur (grade of 3 (6 point scale) or 7 (15 points scale) in the final two highschool years
DAAD certificate, issued by TUM's Language Center (Minimum top two scores in all 3 sections)
Check MQs Language Requirement Website for details
MQs Language Requirement Website
Additional Information
On-campus accommodation is limited and cannot be guaranteed for exchange students
Accessibility and disability support should be arranged at the time of enrolment at MQ.
Accessibility and disability support

Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Campus
Brisbane
Semester Dates
Semester 2: July to November
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Semester 1: February to June
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
Study cycles are broadly similar to the German structure (Bachelor/Master).
Continuous Assessment: Weekly essays, presentations, mid-term exams, etc. account for 40–60% of the final grade.
Large lectures and small seminars (tutorials or labs): Attendance and active participation are expected/graded.
Standard load at QUT is four units per semester (48 credit points)
Units are classed as either 'approved' or 'require approval'.
Approved units don't require prior study, while units need approval typically have prerequisites.
Admission Requirements
GPA of 2.5 on a 4-point scale (or equivalent) ~ 2,5 at TUM
Academic Restrictions
Postgraduate students can't enrol in first-year undergraduate core units or in postgraduate honours-level units
Enrolment in capstone units is generally not allowed for exchange students
Language Requirements
English: B2
IELTS, TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, Cambridge Advanced (CAE), Cambridge Proficiency (CPE)
English Language Certificates, issued by TUM's Language Center
All English Language Test Results have to be taken within the past 2 years
Additional Information
On-campus accommodation is not guaranteed for exchange students
QUT accommodation services provides guidance (see website)

Stays starting in February: November 1 (of previous year)

Semester Dates

Specific Programs
Interested in studying at RMIT's branches in Vietnam? Please select "RMIT Vietnam" in TUM Global's database
Study System
Study cycles are broadly similar to the German structure (Bachelor/Master).
Continuous Assessment: Weekly essays, presentations, mid-term exams, etc. account for 40–60% of the final grade.
Large lectures and small seminars (tutorials or labs): Attendance and active participation are expected/graded.
The maximum study load per semester at RMIT is 48 credit points (usually 4 courses).
Find available courses at RMIT's Study Abroad and Exchange Course Search

Admission Requirements
Minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 out of 4 point scale or 60% average ~ min. 2,7 at TUM
Language Requirements
English: B2
Students from RMIT Exchange partners are not required to submit proof of an English language competency.
Additional Information
On-campus accommodation not guaranteed for exchange students

Undergraduate / Bachelor

Website
Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Campus
Brisbane, St. Lucia Campus
Semester Dates
Semester 2: July to November
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Semester 1: February to June
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
Study cycles are broadly similar to the German structure (Bachelor/Master).
Continuous Assessment: Weekly essays, presentations, mid-term exams, etc. account for 40–60% of the final grade.
Large lectures and small seminars (tutorials or labs): Attendance and active participation are expected/graded.
A standard full-time load at UQ is 4 courses per semester.
To search for available courses, check UQ's course catalogue
UQ's course catalogue
Language Requirements
English: C1
Official certificate from TUM Language Center, certifying CEFR C1 level English language proficiency
German Abitur with a minimum grade of 2 (good / 10 Punkte) or better in English
IELTS (min. 6.5 overall and min. 6.0 in each sub-band) or acceptable scores in equivalent tests
TOEFL: UQ has not adopted the new 1–6 scoring model. UQ therefore only accepts TOEFL iBT Australia with section scores reported on a 0–30 scale. TOEFL iBT with section scores reported on a 1–6 scale, TOEFL iBT Home Edition, TOEFL ITP are not recognised by UQ.
For major details, check UQs Entry Requirements Website
acceptable scores in equivalent testsUQs Entry Requirements Website
Additional Information
On-Campus accommodation is not guaranteed for exchange students but UQ Accommodation Service assists you with finding a suitable home before arriving in Brisbane.
UQ provides free support, services and facilities for students with a disability, illness, injury or mental health condition.
UQ Ally is UQ's program for the LGBTQIA+ community
UQ Accommodation Servicestudents with a disability, illness, injury or mental health conditionUQ Ally
Application Deadlines at Host University
For stays starting in July: February 28
For stays in February: September 30 (of previous year)

University of New South Wales (UNSW) Sydney · AustraliaShow 13 information sections: languages, deadlines, semester dates and moreHide detailed information BachelorMaster

Undergraduate / Bachelor

Website
Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Partner Information
Fact Sheet 2026/27
Fact Sheet 2026/27
Campus
Sydney
Semester Dates
Term 3: September to December
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Term 1: February to May
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Term 2: June to August
- usually not suitable for TUM student
The current UNSW academic calendar consists of three terms. In addition there is a summer term (ST) in January and a winter term (WT) in August. Exchange students from TUM have the choice of 3 courses over a standard Term, or 4 courses over a double or Tailored Term. For details, check UNSW Fact Sheet.
UNSW Fact Sheet
Study System
Study cycles are broadly similar to the German structure (Bachelor/Master).
Continuous Assessment: Weekly essays, presentations, mid-term exams, etc. account for 40–60% of the final grade.
Classes are the teaching sessions that make up a course. Classes can include lectures, seminars, tutorials and lab sessions.
Attendance and active participation during classes are expected/graded
Every course at UNSW is measured in Units of Credit (UOC).
International students need to enrol in a minimum of 12 UOC each term to be considered full-time.
Admission Requirements
Credit average or a 3.0 out of 4.0 GPA ~ 2,5 at TUM
Academic Restrictions
Most courses are open to exchange students who meet the required academic background
Course restrictions are listed in UNSW Fact Sheet.
Generally undergraduate students are not able to enrol in postgraduate courses except limited options for some Science and Engineering subjects.
It is generally not possible for postgraduate students to enrol in undergraduate courses.
UNSW Fact Sheet
Language Requirements
English: B2
IELTS (6.5 overall score) and TOEFL (90 overall score): test must be completed max. two years before the start date at UNSW
German Abitur with minimum grade 12 in English, undertaken max. ten years prior to the start date at UNSW
At least one consecutive year of full-time study at Bachelor level or higher where English was the sole language of instruction and assessment. Certificate to be provided by respective TUM department.
Additional Information
In-person compulsory orientation, normally held the week before Term starts.
On campus accommodation is extremely limited and is not guaranteed even if you apply by the deadline.
Most exchange students choose to live off campus and enjoy the beautiful suburbs that surround UNSW.
UNSW Off-Campus Accommodation provides advice. Arrive at least two weeks prior to semester start, to find suitabe housing.
Equitable Learning Services provide a range of services to students with disabilities
UNSW Off-Campus AccommodationEquitable Learning Services
Application Deadlines at Host University
For stays starting in September: April 1
For stays starting in February: October 1 (of previous year)

Exchange Information
Campus
Sydney
Semester Dates
Semester 2: July to November
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Semester 1: February to June
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
Study cycles are broadly similar to the German structure (Bachelor/Master).
Continuous Assessment: Weekly essays, presentations, mid-term exams, etc. account for 40–60% of the final grade.
Large lectures and small seminars (tutorials or labs): Attendance and active participation are expected/graded.
Standard full-time workload at USYD for exchange students: 24 credit points per semester, which usually equals four units of study (6 credit points each).
Check USYD's Unit of Study Tool
USYD's Unit of Study Tool
Admission Requirements
CGPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 point scale, or an average grade of ‘C’ or better on the European ECTS grading scale
Language Requirements
English: C1
IELTS (6.5 overall score), TOEFL iBT, Cambridge. Tests need to be no more than two years old at the date of course commencement.
C1-level English Language Certificate from TUM (Language Center)
German Abitur (min. 8 points) achieved max. 10 years before commencing courses at USYD
One year of full-time study (or part-time equivalent) in a recognised bachelor’s degree where the instruction for your studies (teaching, assessment and examination) was entirely in English
Additional Information
Guaranteed accommodation in student accommodation buildings within a 20 minute walk of campus

University of Technology Sydney (UTS) Sydney · AustraliaShow 12 information sections: languages, deadlines, semester dates and moreHide detailed information BachelorMaster

Undergraduate / Bachelor

Website
Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Campus
Sydney
Semester Dates
Semester 2: July to November
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Semester 1: February to June
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
Study cycles are broadly similar to the German structure (Bachelor/Master).
Continuous Assessment: Weekly essays, presentations, mid-term exams, etc. account for 40–60% of the final grade.
Large lectures and small seminars (tutorials or labs): Attendance and active participation are expected/graded.
Full-time study load at UTS: 18 to 24 credit points per semester ~ enrolling in 3 to 4 subjects per semester.
Step by step guide on how to explore subjects at UTS
Step by step guide on how to explore subjects at UTS
Admission Requirements
Equivalent to a 65% Weighted Average Mark (WAM) ~ minimum 3,0 at TUM.
At least 60 ECTS at the time of application at UTS.
For Postgraduate applications, completion of Bachelor program is required.
Language Requirements
English: B2
IELTS, TOEFL, PTE and Cambridge Certificate.
German Abitur (minimum mark 7 in year 12 & 13)
Proof of minimum one year of full-time study in a study program at TUM, taught entirely in English. Provide written proof from your TUM department!
UTS English Language Proficiency Assessment (ELPA): Please forward this form to your TUMexchange coordinator at TUM Global Office together with a proof of your English proficiency. Do not forward this form to TUM Language Center!
UTS does not accept the DAAD Language Certificate
For details, please check UTS website
UTS website
Additional Information
UTS Housing offers a limited number of beds at UTS'S on-campus student residence "Yura Mudang" for exchange students.
There is a non-refundable application fee of AUD$50 for Yura Mudang, even if you are unsuccessful in securing a place.
UTS recommends that students investigate off-campus accommodation options at the same time as applying to Yura Mudang.
Application Deadlines at Host University
Stays starting in July: March 31
Stays starting in February: October 31 (of previous year)

Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Semester Dates
Semester 2: July to November
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Semester 1: February to June
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
Study cycles are broadly similar to the German structure (Bachelor/Master).
Continuous Assessment: Weekly essays, presentations, mid-term exams, etc. account for 40–60% of the final grade.
Large lectures and small seminars (tutorials or labs): Attendance and active participation are expected/graded.
Each UOW subject is worth 6 credit points. A fulltime study load is typically 3 subjects (18 credit points) or 4 subjects (24 credit points).
For more information visit the UOW Handbook
UOW Handbook
Admission Requirements
A cumulative grade point average (GPA) of 2.7 or higher on a 4.0 scale ~ 3,0 at TUM
Language Requirements
English: B2
IELTS (6.0), TOEFL, Cambridge Advanced
German Abitur
Certificate from TUM Language Center
Certificates from any official English language test centers, certifying B2-level
Additional Information
On-campus accommodation is guaranteed for exchange students. Make sure to apply at UOW Living on time.
Complimentary airport pick-up available upon request.
Orientation attendance is compulsory.
Application Deadlines at Host University
Stays starting in July: April 1
Stays starting in February: October 1 (of previous year)

Study System
The first cicle in Brazil, the Graduacao (Bachelor), lasts four to six years. Master's students can attend courses at an advanced Graduacao level.
The second cicle, Mestrado or Especializacao, is not equivalent to the German Master system and not open to student exchange.
Language Requirements
Portuguese
UNICAMP does not require prior knowledge of Portuguese. However, for a successful participation in courses taught in Portuguese, TUM requires at least a A2, better a B1 level in Portuguese.

Study System
The first cicle in Brazil, the Graduacao (Bachelor), lasts four to six years. Master's students can attend courses at an advanced Graduacao level.
The second cicle, Mestrado or Especializacao, is not equivalent to the German Master system and not open to student exchange.
Students from engineering disciplines will be nominated to the Escola Politécnica.
Students from the TUM School of Social Sciences and Technology apply to the Centro de Filosofia e Ciencias Humanas or the School of Communication.

Minimum CGPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) / B average ~ min. 2,5 at TUM
Academic Restrictions
Exchange at McGill is only open for TUM bachelor students.
Biochemistry and Biomedical Engineering at McGill is not open for exchange students.
TUM master students cannot apply for McGill as admission to graduate programs is highly restricted and rejections are very common.
TUM master students cannot take undergraduate courses at McGill.
Limited spaces in all Engineering disciplines; supplemental fees possible for particular courses.
Students should apply for the same the same program at McGill where they are enrolled at TUM OR must present sufficient background in chosen subject area.
Language Requirements
English:
McGill accepts certificates, issued by TUM Language Center or official tests (TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge).
Highschool certificates (Abitur) is not accepted!
Application Deadlines at Host University
For stays starting in September: April 1st
For stays starting in January: October 1 (of previous year)

Level
Undergraduate / Bachelor

Website
Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Campus
Edmonton Campus: Main Campus
Augustana Campus: Camrose, 100 km south of Edmonton; courses offered there have the code starting with "AU"
Semester Dates
Fall Term: September to December
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Winter Term: January to May
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Admission Requirements
Cumulative GPA equivalent to at least a 2.5 on a 4.0 scale ~ min. 2,5 at TUM
Graduate-level exchange:
have completed your undergraduate degree,
be registered in a graduate-level program,
have grade results from at least one semester/term in your graduate program.
Some UAlberta faculties have other requirements - check partner's website
check partner's website
Academic Restrictions
Undergraduate students cannot take graduate-level courses (usually numbered 500 or higher)
Graduate students cannot take undergraduate-level courses (usually numbered below 500)
Course availability is not guaranteed: Choose courses aligned with your academic background and prepare alternative courses as backup
High-Demand Departments: Art & Design, Computing Science, Economics (=highly unlikely to take many (if any) courses
Undergraduate exchange students must take all or a majority of their courses in the same department
Graduate exchange students must list courses from only one department
Language Requirements
English
TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo - check fact sheet for details.
German Abitur: grade of "Gut" (Note 2) or better in A-level English
Additional Information
On-campus housing is guaranteed to all exchange students beginning in September and apply on time
No on-housing guarantee for exchange students beginning in January
Research at UAlberta
Undergraduate students: Cannot conduct research.
Graduate students: Can take courses or conduct research, but not both. Research requires finding a UAlberta supervisor before applying.
Application Deadlines at Host University
For stays starting in September: March 1st
For stays starting in January: September 1st (of previous year)

University of British Columbia (UBC) Vancouver · CanadaShow 13 information sections: languages, deadlines, semester dates and moreHide detailed information BachelorMaster
20 eligible subject areas, listed belowChecked 2026-09-16
Level
Undergraduate / Bachelor
Postgraduate / Master
Website
Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Campus
Vancouver
Okanagan
Semester Dates
Term 1: September to December
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Term 2: January to May
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
Bachelor/undergraduate study cycle: 4 years
Master/graduate study cycle: 1-3 years (research-based or course-based)
Admission Requirements
GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale ~ min. 2,5 at TUM
Academic Restrictions
Limited availability in graduate-level courses (=500+ level) and separate approval process
TUM master students can apply for an undergraduate program at UBC and choose upper-level undergraduate courses (=300 & 400 level).
No research-stays possible
Graduate level courses in political science and economics at UBC’s Faculty of Arts and at Sauder School of Business are not available to exchange students
Very limited capacity at computer science (CPSC) courses
Undergraduate CPSC courses (200-level and up) only open to students majoring in computer science at TUM with required prerequisites
Faculty of Applied Science (Engineering) is only open to students pursuing a degree in engineering at TUM
Language Requirements
English: B2
Test results must be no more than two years old at the time of application to UBC.
Accepted Certificates: Cambridge, TOEFL, TOEFL iBt, IELTS, PTE, DET
Check this website for details: https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/coming-ubc-exchange/english-language-requirements-coming-ubc-exchange
https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/coming-ubc-exchange/english-language-requirements-coming-ubc-exchange
Additional Information
Vancouver Campus: On-campus housing not guaranteed. Exchange students should apply as soon as students receive their UBC ID number. $50 non-refundable application fee.
Okanagan Campus: On-campus housing prioritized for exchange students. 90% housing placement rate.
Application Deadlines at Host University
For stays starting in September or January: April 1st

Level
Undergraduate / Bachelor
Campus
Winnipeg
Semester Dates
Term 1: September to December
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Term 2: January to May
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Admission Requirements
Undergraduate admission is not too competitive; no strict GPA
Graduate-level admission (Master) is competitive; completion of a four-year undergraduate program is required.
Academic Restrictions
TUM students can only apply for undergraduate level courses at U Manitoba.
TUM master studets who completed a three-year bachelor program cannot access Graduate-level courses at U Manitoba.
TUM master students can apply for Manitoba's undergraduate program to take courses at 1000 to 4000 level (highest).
Students from TUM School of Management have to apply via SOMex for U Manitoba.
Students from TUM Landscape Architecture and from TUM Architecture have to apply via their TUM school for Manitoba.
Language Requirements
English
U Manitoba only accepts TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge or Duolingo (see Fact Sheet for details) as proof.
Additional Information
On-Campus Housing is available for exchange students - usually enough capacity (=almost guaranteed)
Application Deadlines at Host University
For stays starting in September or January: April 15

Exchange Information

Fact Sheet 2026/27
Fact Sheet 2026/27
Campus
St. George Campus (UTSG): Arts&Science; Applied Science&Engineering; Architecture,Landscape&Design, etc.
Scarborough Campus (UTSC): Mainly Humanities, Social Sciences, Science and Management but also Computer Science
Mississauga Campus (UTM): Mainly Humanities, Social Sciences, Science and Management but also Computer Science
Semester Dates
Fall Term: September to December
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Winter Term: January to May
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Specific Programs
TUM master students, wishing to be involved in research activities at U of T will be admitted under the International Visiting Graduate Students program (IVGS)
IVGS is not automatically included in the TUMexchange options and there might be additional fees
Please contact your TUMexchange Advisor at TUM Global Office, in case you are interested in this option - application dates and conditions are different!
Admission Requirements
Academic requirements (including GPA) differ per faculty and vary based on the agreement with the partner institution: Carefully check incoming website at U Toronto !!!
At U of T, undergraduate program lasts 4 years. TUM students in the first year of their graduate/master program should apply as an undergraduate student for exchange at U of T!
Graduate exchange applications are considered on an individual basis by each graduate unit. Meeting the minimum eligibility does not guarantee admission.
incoming website at U Toronto
Academic Restrictions
Carefully review the list of restricted programs and courses on TUM student's incoming website at U Toronto !!!
The Department of Computer Science at St. George campus will host a very limited number of students. Applicants may be redirected to UTSC or UTM
At Scarborough and Mississauga Campus, only undergraduate-level-courses are open for TUM Management (MGT) students.
Rotman Commerce is not open for exchange studentsfrom TUM!
Language Requirements
English:
UToronto only accepts TOEFL and IELTS
Duolingo English Tests are not accepted at all faculties of U Toronto!!! Check UToronto's Website carefully!
Any other English proficiency tests or examinations for exchange are NOT accepted!!!
Additional Information
Accommodation is not guaranteed for exchange students
Application Deadlines at Host University
Same deadline for fall and winter term
1 March: all graduate applications
1 April: all undergraduate applications

Student Exchange Information
Semester Dates
Semester A (1st semester): end of August to end of November
– corresponds to TUM winter semester
Semester B (2nd semester): mid-January to mid-April
– corresponds to TUM summer semester
Academic Restrictions
courses only at undergraduate (Bachelor’s) level
Master’s students may take undergraduate courses, but must verify credit recognition with their TUM School
Master’s students from TUM School of Management are NOT eligible for exchange
Language Requirements
English proof: TOEFL/IELTS, Abitur (min. 10 points), or DAAD certificate (for details check fact sheet)
Additional Information
No guaranteed on-campus housing; support with off-campus accommodation
Application Deadlines at Host University
Stays starting in August/September: mid-May
Stays starting in January: mid-October

Level
Undergraduate / Bachelor
Postgraduate / Master
Campus
Shanghai
Semester Dates
Fall Semester: September to January
– corresponds to TUM winter semester
Spring Semester: February to July
– corresponds to TUM summer semester
Important: The Global College Program is divided into trimesters : Fall: Sep-Dec / Spring: Feb-Apr / Summer: Mai-Aug, therefore for fall, please enter “Wintersemester” in the TUMexchange application form / for Spring or Summer, or Spring and Summer together, please enter “Sommersemester” in the application form and specify in your motivation letter
Specific Programs
1.) General Program
For students of all TUM faculties, except:
• Informatics
• Master’s students of the TUM School of Management
• Courses from the School of Medicine and the Shanghai Advanced Institute of Finance are not available to exchange students.
https://global.sjtu.edu.cn/en/study-sjtu/prospective/non-degree-programs/281
Fact Sheet 2026-27: https://sjtu.feishu.cn/docx/EiC8dmC0jocFVGxM2hncJ2bWnFf
2.) Global College (formerly Joint Institute)
Only for students from:
• TUM School of Engineering & Design (except architecture)
• Electrical and Computer Engineering
• Informatics
https://global.sjtu.edu.cn/en/study-sjtu/prospective/non-degree-programs/281
Fact Sheet 2026-27: https://sjtu.feishu.cn/docx/EiC8dmC0jocFVGxM2hncJ2bWnFf
3.) ACEM (Antai College of Economics and Management)
Only for Master’s students of the TUM School of Management
a) Master of International Business
• No prior work experience required
• Exchange students can only take courses within this program
b) MBA Program
• At least three years of work/internship experience required
• Exchange students can only take courses within this program
https://global.sjtu.edu.cn/en/study-sjtu/prospective/non-degree-programs/281https://sjtu.feishu.cn/docx/EiC8dmC0jocFVGxM2hncJ2bWnFfhttps://global.sjtu.edu.cn/en/study-sjtu/prospective/non-degree-programs/281https://sjtu.feishu.cn/docx/EiC8dmC0jocFVGxM2hncJ2bWnFf
Admission Requirements
Exchange students with Chinese citizenship are not accepted
Language Requirements
English: B2

• Official language certificates: TOEFL, IELTS,
Cambridge Certificate

• DAAD certificate issued by the TUM Language Center

ANTAI College of Economics and Management: Fall: April

only Master's students can take courses from the "Data Science" master's program and from the PhD/MPhil program in "Computer and Information Engineering"
Language Requirements
minimum TOEFL score of 530 (paper-based) / 71 (internet-based) (TOEFL 1–6 scale: 3.5) or IELTS 6.0 or equivalent

maximum credit load per term is 18 (no exceptions)
only 12 to 15 credits recommended, to leave time for exploring the local community and city
recommended not to take the full course load within the majors, workload can be intense and course enrollment may not always be successful

Course Catalogue
Academic Restrictions
courses only at undergraduate (Bachelor’s) level
Master’s students may take undergraduate courses, but must verify credit recognition with their TUM School
flexible study plan required as enrollment into classes is subject to constraints such as class quota, pre-requisite requirements, instructors’ consent, etc. (especially regarding computation and AI courses)
students are allowed to take courses offered by other Schools, but enrollment priority in non-engineering courses will be lower
Language Requirements
no English Proof required, but it is expected that your level corresponds to the levels mentioned in the factsheet
Additional Information
on-campus accommodation cannot be guaranteed
arrangement of private accomodation may be necessary
maximum credit load per term is 18 (no exceptions). Recommendation: enroll in 12–15 credits to leave time for exploring the local community and city.
Students should not expect to take a full course load within their majors, as the workload can be intense and course enrollment may not always be successful.
Students should consider also non-major electives such as courses in the arts, humanities, languages, or social sciences.
Due to high demand for COMP and AI courses, students are advised to remain flexible with their study plans.
Course enrollment cannot be guaranteed in general.

Stays starting in September: March
Stays starting in February: September

Academic Restrictions
At Coller School of Management, only students in a Master's level from TUM School of Management can be accepted. A TOEFL or IELTS English proficiency is mandatory.

Medicine students can enroll at the School of Graduate Studies and School of Public Health. The Gray School of Medicine, the School of Health Orofessions and the School of Dental Medicine are restricted and not open for course enrollment.

Specific Programs
YSEP (Young Science and Engineering Researchers Program):
Research program for Master’s students or Bachelor’s students who have completed at least 5 semesters.
ACAP (Academic Course Access Program):
mainly only for Master's level students
Bachelor's level students in their final year may take courses for graduates, if they are explicitly open for undergraduate-level International Exchange Students (

Semester Dates
Fall Semester: Mid-September to early February

Specific Programs
KIP Keio International program: for Bachelor and Master
Graduate Studies Program (GSP): for Master's degree students who wish to take graduate-level courses through affiliation with a Graduate School of Keio University
KIP@SFC” (Keio International Program @Shonan Fujisawa Campus): This program allows students to reside in Keio University dormitories located at or near the SFC campus and take courses offered exclusively at SFC. Please note that due to the distance (approximately 1.5 hours) between SFC and Tokyo, students enrolled in KIP@SFC are not permitted to take courses at other campuses.

Factsheet
Factsheet
Semester Dates
Fall Semester: September to February
– corresponds to TUM winter semester
Spring Semester: April to August
– corresponds to TUM summer semester
Specific Programs
OUSSEP: for Bachelor's or Master's students, however most courses offered are at Bachelor's level, OUSSEP students primarily take International Exchange Subjects, which consist of a range of liberal arts courses for 2nd- and 3rd-year undergraduate students (TUM Bachelor's students need to be at least in their 5th semester during exchange)
FrontierLab: research stay for Bachelor's or Master's students in laboratories of the following schools or their departments: Science, Engineering Science, Engineering, Information Science and Technology. Participants can also take international exchange subjects and Japanese language and other related subjects
iExPO (Immersion Exchange Program Osaka): only if your Japanese level is at least B1/B2 (CEFR)/ N2 (JLPT)
MAPLE (Intensive Japanese Language and Culture Program for Exchange Students): only if your Japanese level is at least A2 (CEFR)/ N4 (JLPT) and only for 2 semester stays with beginning in September
Admission Requirements
GPA-Requirement: at least 2.0 (German scale) by the time of both the TUMexchange application and the direct application at the partner university
Language Requirements
TOEFL iBT 80 / IELTS 6.0 or higher
Cambridge English with CEFR B2 level or higher
Official assessment report (on both receptive and productive skills) of home university’s language center
Official certificate/letter which proves English is the medium of instruction at student’s faculty
Application Deadlines at Host University
Stays starting in September: Mid-March
Stays starting in April: Mid-October

Factsheet
Factsheet
Semester Dates
Winter Semester: October to March
– corresponds to TUM winter semester
Summer Semester: April to September
– corresponds to TUM summer semester
Admission Requirements
only for Master's students from TUM School of Computation, Information and Technology (CIT) or from Physics
no official GPA-requirement; due to high demand, a GPA of at least 2.0 (German scale) at the time of the TUMexchange application is strongly recommended
every student needs to find a laboratory under a supervising professor, start searching immediately after you have been accepted (indicate also your exchange semester)
do not contact any professors before you have been accepted for TUMexchange
if your exchange begins in the following Winter term, start looking for a supervising professor as soon as you have been accepted for TUMexchange
Language Requirements
No English language proof required
Additional Information
Students whose primary focus is coursework are still welcome, provided that they also participate in some form of research in a laboratory.
All exchange students required to register for the IST Project Research course and to submit a three-page report on their research work at the end of each semester.
IST Project Research course

Spring Semester: late March to early August
– corresponds to TUM summer semester
Specific Programs
COLABS: Research stay only for Master's students, consists of Core course (Individual Research Training in Lab) and Elective courses
JYPE (Junior Year Program in English): only available for Fall term, only for Bachelor's students
IPLA (International Program in Liberal Arts): only available for Fall term and only for Bachelor's students from the TUM School of Management. Please note, only a very limited number of English-taught courses can be recognised at TUM SoM. Be sure to double-check with the internatioal advisors at the TUM School of Management.
DEEP (Direct Enrollment Education Program for Natural Science Students): all courses in Japanese, only for Bachelor's students with mandatory JAPANESE NATIVE SPEAKER LEVEL (JLPT N1)
Language Requirements
see Factsheet
Application Deadlines at Host University
Important note for COLABS participants: If you have been selected for COLABS, do not wait for an official nomination. Please, begin the official prior consent application process to find an academic supervisor as early as possible (for stays starting in Fall usually end November/ early December, for stays starting in Spring usually in July). However, it is strictly forbidden to contact potential supervisors directly. Be sure to study the detailed COLABS application procedure thoroughly.
Application Deadlines for all programs
Stays starting in September: Mid-February
Stays starting in March: Mid-November

Semester Dates
Semester 3: September to December
-corresponds to TUM winter semester
Semester 1: January to April
-corresponds to TUM summer semester
Semester 2: May to August
-corresponds to TUM summer semester
The academic year is divided into 2 or 3 cycles. Please check the detailed academic calendar of your prefered JKUAT School.
Admission Requirements
Application documents for JKUAT:
Transcrip of Records
CV
Recommendation letter from TUM professor or post-doc
Language Requirements
English
JKUAT does not require an English proficiency. However, TUM recommends to have at least a B2 level in English.
Additional Information
Accommodation: on-campus accommodation (single or double bedroom; shared kitchen and living room)
Exchange students who stay longer than three months need an immigration pass.
TUM SEED Center has cooperation with JKUAT and a living lab. For more details, please visit the SEED website.
Application Deadlines at Host University
There are no official deadlines from JKUAT. For this reason, we set TUM deadlines for organizational reasons.

Stays starting in May: End of January

Exchange Information
Semester Dates
Fall Semester: September to December

Admission Requirements
GPA Requirement Bachelor's students: at least 2.5 (German scale) both at the time of the TUMexchange application and the application at the partner university
GPA Requirement Master's students: at least 2.0 (German scale) both at the time of the TUMexchange application and the application at the partner university
Academic Restrictions
not available as host department: Dept. of Computer Science and Engineering, Dept. of Electrical and Computer Engineering
students from these departments are strongly advised to focus on elective courses
please carefully study further restrictions in the factsheet
to enroll in Master's courses at the host university, you must have completed at least one Master's semester at TUM by the application deadline at SNU
Language Requirements
no English language proof required
Additional Information
Once you apply at SNU after your nomination from TUM, you need to state 3 Department Preferences. You may not be granted your first choice.

Semester Dates
Fall semester: August to December
-corresponds to TUM winter semester
Spring semester: February to June
-corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
The first cicle in Mexico, the Licenciatura (Bachelor), lasts four to six years. Master's students attend courses at an advanced Licenciatura level.
ITESM has a course offer in Spanish and English, offer veries according to the subject area.
There is no guarantee to participate in English taught courses only.
1 Tec Credit > 1,67 ECTS > 1 USA Credit
Preliminary Course Catalog
Academic Restrictions
Management students can only select courses on a Licenciatura level.
Language Requirements
Spanish
For courses taught in Spanish: B1 (Spanish Placement Test before selection of courses)
English
For courses taught in English: B1 (see accepted language proficiencies in Fact Sheet)
Additional Information
Accommodation:
-Residence halls in Guadalajara, Monterrey, Puebla and Querétaro
-Host family in Ciudad de México, Guadalajara, Monterrey, and Querétaro
-Self-organized housing in all locations

Study System
The first cicle in Mexico, the Licenciatura (Bachelor), lasts four to six years. Master's students attend courses at an advanced Licenciatura level.
At UNAM, TUM master students can also enroll in the Master/Graduate program (Posgrado), please check the organization details as Masters are organized differently in Latin America.
Admission Requirements
GPA undergraduate programs: 8/10 ~ TUM grade average of 2,6
minimum of 44% adcanve on credits and courses

Semester Dates

-corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
The first cicle in Mexico, the Licenciatura (Bachelor), lasts four to six years. Master's students attend courses at an advanced Licenciatura level.
UDLAP has a course offer in Spanish and English, offer varies according to the subject area.
There is no guarantee to participate in English taught courses only.
1 UDLAP Credit = 1 ECTS
Preliminary Course Catalog
Language Requirements
Spanish B2
For courses taught in Spanish:
DAAD certificate from TUM Language Center
Undergraduate students from a non-native Spanisch speaking country must addiditionally participate in the UDLAP Online Spanish Proficiency Test.
English B2
For courses taught in English:
TOEFL IBT, IELTS
DAAD certificate from TUM Language Center
If you want to enroll in Spanish and English taught courses, you must hand in a proficiency for both languages.
Additional Information
Amigos Internacionales
Orientation week
Accommodation: On campus (Residential Colleges, not guaranteed) or off campus (private housing)
Application Deadlines at Host University
Stays starting in August: Mid of May
Stays starting in February: Mid of October

Semester Dates
Semester 1 (Fall): August to December
-corresponds to TUM winter semester
Semester 2 (Spring): January to May
-corresponds to TUM summer semester
Specific Programs
Global Connect Fellowship
Programme period: 1 July – 31 August
Application period: 15 January – 15 February
Application process: Apply directly via the programme website or contact the TUMexchange coordinator for Singapore by 31 January to receive an official TUM nomination and priority consideration. Nominations are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.
Eligibility: Bachelor's and master's students, preferably in STEM disciplines, who are expected to graduate within the next year and have a strong interest in research and/or pursuing a PhD at NTU. A good academic record is required.
Programme benefits: SGD 5,000 research scholarship for a two-month research placement, fully funded on-campus accommodation, faculty mentorship, masterclasses, professional development seminars, networking opportunities, and a final poster presentation.
Important: The GCF Programme is independent of a regular NTU exchange semester through TUMexchange. Participation in one programme does not require participation in the other.
GEM Trailblazer Summer (NTU Summer School)
Programme period:
2-week sessions (Track 2: Entrepreneurship & Innovation only):
Session 1: 22 June – 4 July 2026
Session 2: 5 July – 18 July 2026
4-week session (all other tracks): 22 June – 18 July 2026
Application period: 15 February – 31 March
Application process: Students must be nominated by the TUM Global Office. To be considered for nomination, please email the TUMexchange Singapur coordinator by February 2027. Please note that TUM can only nominate students for participation on a fee-paying basis.
Eligibility: Undergraduate students from all disciplines at TUM with a minimum GPA of 2.5/5.0 (or 2.0/4.0) who meet NTU’s English language requirements.
Important: Participation is subject to nomination by TUM and final admission by NTU.
Study System
The Bachelor in Singapore lasts three to four years, while the Master lasts one to two years.
Admission Requirements
GPA of at least 3,3/5 ~ GPA of 2,5 at TUM
English proficiency
Academic Restrictions
Only bachelor's students are eligible to apply for an exchange semester at NTU. Exchange students may only enrol in undergraduate-level courses at NTU.
As part of the application process, exchange students must indicate at least 10 courses per semester in their preliminary course selection. At least 50% of these courses must be offered by the school corresponding to the selected “Equivalent NTU Programme”.
Course enrollment is subject to approval by the respective NTU school(s) and is based on the student’s academic background and prerequisites. Students are therefore strongly advised to remain flexible regarding their course choices.
Exchange students are not permitted to enroll in restricted courses or programmes. Please refer to NTU’s Fact Sheet for a list of restricted courses.
NTU’s College of Computing and Data Science (CCDS): Despite the capacity restrictions outlined in NTU’s Fact Sheet, TUM may nominate a limited number of students from TUM Informatics for exchange at CCDS. The number of available places is agreed annually between TUM and NTU.

English

Campus
Singapore
Semester Dates
Semester 1: August to December
-corresponds to TUM winter semester
Semester 2: January to May
-corresponds to TUM summer semester
Specific Programs
NUS Young Fellowship Programme
Programme period: 1-week on-site research programme (mid/end June) + mandatory online presentation (end of July)
Application process: Nomination by TUM Global is requiered. Please send your interest to the TUMexchange coordinator for Singapore.
Eligibility: Bachelor's students from all disciplines at TUM, 3rd semester or higher
Programme focus: Research experience and insight into graduate studies at NUS
Important: The NUS Young Fellowship Programme is independent of the semester-long exchange through TUMexchange. Participation in one programme does not require participation in the other.
Study System
The study system in Singapore is quite simular to the TUM system. The Bachelor / Undergraduae cycle lasts three to four years and the Masters / Postgraduate cycle lasts one to two years. Between these to cicles, there is additionally the Honours year.
Exchange students may enroll in courses with NUS course codes from 1000-4000, subject to prerequisites, availability, and faculty approval. Masters students shall enroll in advanced Undergraduate courses with NUS course code 4000.
Admission Requirements
GPA with a B average ~ TUM GPA of 2,3
No grade should be below C ~ 2,7 at TUM
English proficiency
Academic Restrictions
Masters students shall enroll in advanced Undergraduate courses with NUS course code 4000.
Level 5000-6000 course codes are postgraduate courses and restricted for exchange.
Language Requirements
English
NUS does not requiere an English Language Proficiency from exchange students. However, you should have at least a B2 level to exchange successfully at NUS.
Additional Information
Accommodation: on-campus cousing (not guaranteed), self-organized
Manditory health insurance conditions
There is a fixed quota of exchange spots per semester at NUS. Being flexible to exchange in semester 1 or 2 might increase your chances to be selected.
Additional visa option: Work-Holiday-Pass
Application Deadlines at Host University
Stays starting in August: Beginning of April
Stays starting in January: Mid of September

Georgia Institute of Technology (Georgia Tech) Atlanta · United StatesShow 12 information sections: languages, deadlines, semester dates and moreHide detailed information Bachelor

Level
Undergraduate / Bachelor
Website
Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Campus
Atlanta
Semester Dates
Fall semester: August to December
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Spring semester: January to May
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
Study cycles are similar to German system: Bachelor/Master
Standard 15-week semester system (Fall and Spring) plus an abbreviated Summer term
Minimum Full-Time course load: 12 credit hours
One credit hour equals 50 minutes of instruction per week
Academic Restrictions
Only undergraduate level courses at Georgia Tech are open to incoming exchange students from TUM
Course catalog is avalable on OSCAR
Students register for courses during Exchange FASET orientation
FASET orientation occurs on the Thursday before the semester begins.
OSCARFASETFASET
Language Requirements
English: C1
TOEFL (minimum iBT 95), Institute Code for TOEFL is 5248
IELTS (minimum 7.0)
Note that a TOEFL/IELTS score report is valid for 2 years max.
No other language certificates are accepted at Georgia Tech.
Additional Information
Orientation Week is mandatory for exchange students (=one week before classes start)
On-campus housing is limited and not guaranteed
Exchange students can apply for on-campus housing at: I-House (GT’s International Living Learning Community)
Students should apply for I-House before they receive official admission to Georgia Tech.
Application Deadlines at Host University
For stays starting in August: April 1
For stays starting in January: October 1 (of previous year)

University of California, Davis (UC Davis) Davis · United StatesShow 13 information sections: languages, deadlines, semester dates and moreHide detailed information BachelorMaster

Undergraduate / Bachelor

Website
Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Campus
Davis
Semester Dates
Fall quarter: September to December
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Winter quarter: January to March
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Spring quarter: April to June
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
(Summer Session I: June – July)
(Summer Session II : August – September)
Study System
The academic year is split into three standard 10-week terms (Fall, Winter, and Spring) plus an optional Summer session
A full-time course load at UCSD is a minimum of 12 units (typically 3 classes) per quarter
Admission Requirements
TUM students need to pay tuition fees at UC Davis: ~USD 8,600 per quarter.
UC Davis offers a discount to TUM students, allowing them to enroll in up to 17 UC Davis units instead of the standard 12.
GPA equivalent to a 3.0 on a 4.0 grade scale (B average) ~ min. 2,5 at TUM.
Academic Restrictions
Only the Global Study Program (GSP) is open for exchange students from TUM at UC Davis
The academic year at UC Davis is divided into quarters and sessions.
Prospective GSP students may apply for one session/quarter or combination of different terms. The terms must be consecutive.
TUM students can choose to apply for one quarter, or for two or three consecutive quarters.
Global Study Program
Language Requirements
English
TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge Certificate
DAAD Certificate, issued by TUM Langugae Center
Proof of English Language Course, incl. final exam at TUM, or another university, or at a private language school
Secondary school certificates from a German secondary school (Abitur)
Additional Information
On-campus housing is not available for GSP exchange students
GSP students make their own housing arrangements with guidance from GSP advisors.
Application Deadlines at Host University
For stays starting in September: May 1
For stays starting in January: October 1
For stays starting in April: January 5
(For stays starting in June or August: March 25)

University of California, San Diego (UCSD) San Diego · United StatesShow 12 information sections: languages, deadlines, semester dates and moreHide detailed information BachelorMaster
23 eligible subject areas, listed belowChecked 2026-09-16
Level
Undergraduate / Bachelor
Postgraduate / Master
Website
Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Campus
La Jolla (15 minutes drive from downtown San Diego)
Semester Dates
Fall quarter: September to December
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Winter quarter: January to March
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Spring quarter: April to June
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
The academic year is split into three standard 10-week terms (Fall, Winter, and Spring) plus an optional Summer session
A full-time course load at UCSD is a minimum of 12 units (typically 3 classes) per quarter
Admission Requirements
Exchange students from TUM have to pay tuition fees at UCSD: ~8500 USD per quarter.
Accommodation is not covered by this tuition fee, so you additionally have to pay for off-campus accommodation.
Academic Restrictions
Cooperation between TUM and UCSD only covers the University and Professional Studies - Program (UPS program).
Access to regular course catalog at UCSD is therefore not guarenteed.
UCSD operates on a quarter system, with three academic quarters and two summer sessions per year.
Summer session are not recommended for exchange students.
Students can choose, if they want to apply for just one quarter, or for more quarters.
Language Requirements
English: C1
IELTS, TOEFL,Cambridge
Duolingo English Test (DET)
DAAD Certificate from TUM Language Center
Additional Information
On-campus accommodation is not available to exchange students.
Application Deadlines at Host University
Students shall apply 12-16 weeks before the desired program start-date

Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Campus
Urbana
Semester Dates
Fall semester: August to December
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Spring semester: January to May
- corresponds to TUM summer semeste
Study System
Study cycles are similar to German system: Bachelor/Master
Standard 15-week semester system (Fall and Spring) plus an abbreviated Summer term
Academic Restrictions
Student Exhange Agreement is only valid for programs at UIUC's Grainger College of Engineering (International Programs (IPENG)
Students assigned to Computer Science will be allowed to take 2 CS courses per semester and will be required to meet course pre-requisites
Students assigned to Physics will be allowed to take a maximum of 3 PHYS courses per semester
All engineering exchange students are required to take ENG 398 Grainger Engineering Design Your Experience.
There is no guarantee of course enrollment in any specific course
Language Requirements
English: C1
TOEFL; IELTS or Duolingo
Documentation from academic institution or English language school, confirming sufficient proficiency in English to participate in the exchange program
Additional Information
University Housing cannot be guaranteed for exchange students.
Exchange students can apply to on-campus Private Certified Housing or rent a private apartment.
Application Deadlines at Host University
For stays starting in August: March 15
For stays starting in January: September 15 (of previous year)

Academic Restrictions
Cooperati between TUM and UTA covers UTA's Cockrell School of Engineering only.
Students admitted to the Engineering exchange program may not enroll in business courses.
The Computer Science program at UT Austin can only accommodate a very limited number of exchange students.
Language Requirements
English: B2
IELTS, TOEFL
Certificate from TUM Language Center
Additional Information
Exchange students attending UT Austin usually choose from three types of housing: co-operative houses (co-ops), private dormitories, and apartments.
Space in UT-owned dorms is available, but limited
Application Deadlines at Host University
For stays starting in August: March 1
For stays starting in January: September 1 (of previous year)

Level
Undergraduate / Bachelor
Postgraduate / Master
Website
Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Campus
Blacksburg
Semester Dates
Fall semester: August to December
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Spring semester: January to May
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
Study cycles are similar to German system: Bachelor/Master
Standard 15-week semester system (Fall and Spring) plus an abbreviated Summer term
Exchange students must be enrolled in a minimum of 12 credits with at least 9 credits taken in-person.
Students must be enrolled in a majority of courses within or pertaining to their VT major to maintain visa eligibility.
Academic Restrictions
TUM master students can apply for VT but they are only allowed to enroll in (upper level) undergraduate courses at Virginia Tech. They cannot enroll in master level courses at VT.
Exchange students are not eligible to major in mechanical engineering.
Exchange students who enroll in two or more courses in the Pamplin College of Business will be charged a non-negotiable fee of $1,275 per semester
Language Requirements
English: B2
TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo, etc. (check VT's Fact Sheet for the complete list)
DAAD certificate, issued by TUM's Language Center with a minimum score of B2 **** in each category.
Students who are native English speakers or are exempt from English placement exams.
Additional Information
Orientation Week is mandatory for exchange students
VT cannot guarantee on-campus housing for exchange students, but students may request it during the application process
Application Deadlines at Host University
For stays starting in August: April 1
For stays starting in January: October 1 (of previous year)

Exchange Information
Exchange Information
Campus
Hanoi City Campus
Saigon South Campus (Ho Chi Minh City)
Semester Dates
Semester 2: June to September
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Semester 3: October to January
- corresponds to TUM winter semester
Semester 1: March to May
- corresponds to TUM summer semester
Study System
Study cycles are broadly similar to the German structure (Bachelor/Master).
Continuous Assessment: Weekly essays, presentations, mid-term exams, etc. account for 40–60% of the final grade.
Large lectures and small seminars (tutorials or labs): Attendance and active participation are expected/graded.
The maximum study load per semester at RMIT is 48 credit points (usually 4 courses).
Admission Requirements
A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 out of 4 point scale ~ 2,7 or above st TUM
Language Requirements
English
Teaching Language at RMIT Vietnam is English only
Students from RMIT Exchange partners are not required to submit proof of an English language competency
Application Deadlines at Host University
For stays starting in June or October: March 31
For stays starting in March: October 31 (of previous year)

Semester Dates

Study System
Study cycles are broadly similar to the German structure (Bachelor/Master).
Continuous Assessment: Weekly essays, presentations, mid-term exams, etc. account for 40–60% of the final grade.
Large lectures and small seminars (tutorials or labs): Attendance and active participation are expected/graded.
The minimum full-time study load at SUT is 37.5 credit points (max. is 50)
Most units of study (but not all) equal 12.5 credits, so students may study 3 or 4 classes per semester
Students can mix and match classes across all study areas as long as they meet the prerequisites
